name: Entegris, Inc.

profile.description: Entegris, Inc. is a leading provider of advanced materials and process solutions for the semiconductor and other high-technology industries. The company's products include specialty chemicals and advanced materials (CMP slurries, deposition materials, cleans), microcontamination control solutions (liquid and gas filtration), and advanced materials handling equipment. Formed through the 2022 acquisition of CMC Materials, Entegris serves the world's largest chipmakers including TSMC, Samsung, and Intel. Headquartered in Billerica, Massachusetts, with approximately 7,700 employees worldwide.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Entegris completed the transformative $6.5B acquisition of CMC Materials in 2022, nearly doubling revenue and creating the broadest semiconductor materials portfolio in the industry spanning filtration, deposition, CMP, and advanced materials handling [1][3]. Under Bertrand Loy's 13-year leadership, revenue grew 5x (from ~$600M to $3.2B) and market cap grew 10x. The company also acquired Versum Materials, further expanding its platform. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI-powered products or AI-driven operational efficiencies were identified for Entegris's own operations; the company enables AI chip manufacturing through its materials but does not deploy AI internally in a quantifiable way [2]. Market Share (2/2): Entegris holds category-leading positions in liquid filtration for semiconductor fabs, CMP slurries and pads (post-CMC acquisition), and advanced deposition materials — serving every major chipmaker globally including TSMC, Samsung, Intel, and SK Hynix [1][3]. Product Pipeline (2/2): $700M investment in a new semiconductor R&D center focused on next-generation deposition materials, CMP slurries, and chemical cleans for sub-3nm nodes and advanced packaging [3]. Content per wafer increases structurally at each new technology node, providing visible and growing demand tied to the industry roadmap. R&D Intensity (1/1): The $700M R&D center investment represents top-quartile commitment for the semiconductor materials sector, reflecting sustained R&D spending as a percentage of revenue well above specialty chemical peers [3].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Entegris's mission — 'to help customers improve their productivity, performance, and technology by providing enhanced materials and process solutions for the most advanced manufacturing environments' — is clear and specific to its role in enabling semiconductor advancement [4]. The PACE core values (Passion, Accountability, Customer-focused, Excellence) provide organizational alignment. However, the mission describes what the company does rather than articulating a vision of a better future — it is functional, not inspirational. Community Impact (0/2): Entegris participates in the Department of Energy's Better Buildings Initiative for energy efficiency, but no specific corporate foundation, charitable programs, or community investment with dollar amounts were identified [4]. Employee Retention (1/2): CEO Bertrand Loy received an 81/100 approval rating on Comparably, placing him in the Top 5% of similarly-sized companies, with reviewers describing him as 'open, honest, and always willing to take the time to discuss matters' [2]. His 13-year CEO tenure (retiring August 2025 to Executive Chair) demonstrates leadership stability. Insider Buying (1/2): Bertrand Loy purchased 44,138 shares for approximately $4.3M at $98.11/share in April 2026, demonstrating meaningful personal conviction [4]. However, other insiders sold approximately $15.2M in stock over the same period, creating a mixed insider signal.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on financial metrics. Entegris's D/E of 93% reflects the debt taken on for the $6.5B CMC Materials acquisition, but at 1.42x debt/EBITDA the leverage is manageable [5]. ROE of 6.79% is below the 15% target, depressed by goodwill-laden balance sheet from acquisitions. Revenue growth 5-year CAGR of 11.5% exceeds the 10% target, driven by CMC integration and secular content-per-wafer growth, though YoY revenue declined 1.38% in 2025 during a semiconductor inventory correction [1]. Forward P/E of 35.98 and PEG of 1.60 reflect premium valuation for a high-quality semiconductor franchise — above targets but not extreme for the sector. Profit margin of 8.18% is below the 20% target but improving as CMC integration synergies are realized; adjusted EBITDA margin of 27.8% in Q1 2026 demonstrates underlying profitability strength. The token dividend ($0.40/share, 0.29% yield) is well-covered by the 22.97% payout ratio.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (9/9): Entegris is AI infrastructure — the company provides the physical materials (ultra-pure chemicals, CMP slurries, filtration membranes, deposition precursors) that are essential inputs to manufacturing AI chips at TSMC, Samsung, Intel, and SK Hynix [1][3]. AI literally cannot replace the need for these physical materials; every AI chip requires Entegris products during fabrication. The company is structurally immune to AI disruption because its products are consumed during manufacturing and must be replaced with each wafer. More importantly, AI directly increases demand for Entegris: AI chips are manufactured at the most advanced nodes (3nm, 2nm) where content per wafer — the amount of Entegris materials consumed — is structurally higher. The AI-driven semiconductor supercycle is the single largest demand driver for Entegris's business. Permitting, qualification, and process integration requirements create multi-year switching costs for fab customers. AI Opportunity (1/1): Entegris generates meaningful and growing revenue from AI chip manufacturing. The company's products are critical inputs for every major AI accelerator (NVIDIA H100/B100, AMD MI300, Google TPU) produced at TSMC, Samsung, and Intel fabs, and content per wafer increases at each advanced node transition [3].

infinite_game.summary: Entegris demonstrates several infinite game qualities — a genuine commitment to enabling semiconductor advancement validated by decades of execution, a high-trust culture under Bertrand Loy's 13-year leadership, and courageous acquisition-led growth that transformed the company's scale and capabilities. However, the recent CEO transition, the mission's functional (rather than inspirational) character, and the lack of evidence for competitive learning prevent a higher score. Sinek would appreciate the cultural foundation but note the absence of a truly transcendent purpose.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Entegris's purpose — enabling the most advanced semiconductor manufacturing through materials science excellence — is genuine and has been validated by 20+ years of consistent execution across multiple technology transitions (from 90nm to 3nm and beyond) [3]. The $700M R&D center investment, the CMC Materials acquisition, and the strategic focus on content-per-wafer growth all trace back to this purpose. The cause connects the company's work to something bigger — enabling the computing technology that powers modern life. However, the mission statement itself reads as functional rather than transformative, and the purpose has not been dramatically tested through existential crisis.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (2/2): CEO Bertrand Loy received an 81/100 approval rating from employees, placing him in the Top 5% of similarly-sized companies on Comparably [2]. Reviewers described him as 'open, honest, and always willing to take the time to discuss matters no matter who you were or what your title was' — language that directly maps to Sinek's Circle of Safety concept. Loy's 13-year CEO tenure, 20-year tenure at the company, and the orderly succession plan (transitioning to Executive Chair rather than departing) reflect deep organizational stability and trust. The $4.3M personal stock purchase post-transition further signals commitment.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No specific evidence of an infinite competitive mindset was identified. Entegris's competitive positioning focuses on technology leadership, content-per-wafer growth, and market share gains — finite metrics focused on winning rather than learning. No management commentary was found referencing specific strengths of competitors like DuPont, Shin-Etsu, or JSR that motivate Entegris to improve.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Entegris has evolved meaningfully from its origins as a contamination control company into a comprehensive semiconductor materials platform through the acquisitions of Versum Materials (2019) and CMC Materials (2022), more than tripling revenue and entering entirely new product categories (CMP, advanced deposition) [1]. The expansion from filtration into specialty chemicals represents genuine strategic evolution. However, the core premise — providing materials to semiconductor fabs — has remained constant, making this platform broadening rather than true existential reinvention.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): The $6.5B CMC Materials acquisition in 2022 was a bold, transformative bet that nearly doubled the company's revenue and required taking on significant debt during a period of semiconductor market uncertainty [1]. The $700M R&D center investment demonstrates long-term commitment to capability building over near-term earnings optimization [3]. However, both decisions were made from a position of strength (Entegris was already well-positioned in a growing market), and the semiconductor supercycle reduced the risk of these bets. True courage — investing during downturns or walking away from profitable but misaligned businesses — has not been tested.

investment_thesis: Entegris delivered a solid Q1 2026 with $811.9M revenue (up 5% YoY), adjusted EPS of $0.86 (beating consensus by 15.4%), and adjusted EBITDA margin of 27.8%, while guiding Q2 revenue to approximately $830M and full-year 2026 revenue of $3.42B [1]. The company occupies a structurally advantaged position in the semiconductor supply chain: content per wafer increases at every advanced node transition, creating a built-in growth tailwind as the industry migrates to 3nm, 2nm, and advanced packaging. AI is the most powerful demand driver — every AI accelerator chip (NVIDIA, AMD, Google TPU) requires Entegris materials during fabrication, and AI chips consume more materials per wafer than commodity processors [3]. The $700M R&D center investment positions Entegris to capture the next wave of semiconductor innovation, while the CMC Materials integration continues to generate synergies. With a 5-year revenue CAGR of 11.5%, category-leading positions across filtration, CMP, and deposition materials, and an 81/100 CEO approval rating, Entegris combines quality franchise economics with long-term secular growth.
thesis_continued: The primary concern is valuation and near-term cyclicality. At 35.98x forward P/E and 79.67x trailing P/E, Entegris trades at a significant premium that requires sustained double-digit earnings growth to justify [5]. The PEG of 1.60 is above the 1.0 target, though not unreasonable for a high-quality compounder. Revenue declined 1.38% in 2025 during the semiconductor inventory correction, demonstrating that even secular growth stories face cyclical headwinds. ROE of 6.79% and profit margin of 8.18% remain depressed by the goodwill and debt from the $6.5B CMC acquisition, and full synergy realization is still in progress [5]. D/E of 93% represents meaningful leverage for a specialty materials company. The CEO transition from Bertrand Loy (retiring after 13 years) introduces succession risk, though the orderly handoff to Executive Chair mitigates this. PFAS regulatory risk is a long-tail concern — while Entegris has not been directly targeted, the broader specialty chemicals industry faces increasing scrutiny on PFAS-containing products that could affect the company's product formulations.
key_catalysts: AI-driven semiconductor supercycle increasing content per wafer at advanced nodes (3nm, 2nm, GAA), with AI chips consuming structurally more Entegris materials than commodity processors — management projects $3.74B revenue by 2027
CMC Materials integration synergies continuing to improve margins, with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding toward 30%+ as the full $75M+ synergy target is realized
$700M R&D center investment enabling Entegris to capture next-generation product opportunities in advanced deposition, selective etch, and advanced packaging materials for sub-2nm nodes
key_risks: Forward P/E of 35.98 and trailing P/E of 79.67 embed expectations for sustained double-digit earnings growth — any semiconductor demand slowdown or delayed recovery from the 2025 inventory correction could trigger significant multiple compression

CEO succession risk as Bertrand Loy transitions from CEO to Executive Chair after 13 years — new CEO must maintain the high-trust culture (Top 5% CEO approval) and strategic continuity that drove 5x revenue growth

PFAS regulatory exposure: while not yet directly targeted, Entegris operates in specialty chemicals where PFAS-containing formulations face growing regulatory and litigation risk that could force costly product reformulations or create liability
